title: Shared low-rank recurrent dynamics with task coordinates
hypothesis: A compact recurrent task View over shared dynamical components recovers held-out task compositions with lower complete bytes than independent RNN matrices while preserving long-horizon trajectories and showing component-specific causal sensitivity.
insertion: recurrent transition only: A(m)=A0 + m1*B1 + m2*B2; input and readout are shared and task-independent

task_family.heldout_rule: two diagonal corner tasks held out from all basis/code fitting

development.selection: no hyperparameter tuning; fixed rank-2 known task-coordinate basis

fresh.release_rule: Do not open fresh after native low-rank alias or frozen quality-gate miss.

controls: shared recurrent core without task code
Mirror task coordinates over shared recurrent bases
native additive low-rank recurrent task conditioning with identical factors and codes
metrics: component ablation delta by task factor
pass_gate: Heldout rollout nRMSE <=0.02, at least 25% fewer bytes than independent, stable spectral radius <1, and strict advantage over native low-rank control at matched storage/compute.
fail_gate: FAIL Mirror-specific claim on exact native alias, quality miss, unstable dynamics, or no strict native-control frontier gain.

compute.active_compute: transition and shared readout MAC proxy per recurrent step; report task-code reconstruction separately
compute.runtime: isolated CPU rollout for small synthetic test bank; not throughput evidence

boundaries: Synthetic linear recurrent dynamics only; no trained RNN, task benchmark, or language-model result.
Heldout diagonal task compositions are excluded from shared-basis and coefficient fitting.
Task coordinates are given by known factor labels; no task inference is claimed.
Mirror and native low-rank share the same mathematical parameterization, intentionally testing attribution rather than assuming a distinct mechanism.
